name: LinkedIn
summary: Sign-in and posting to your own profile are self-serve. Anything an agent typically wants, such as managing company pages, comments, or analytics, sits behind LinkedIn's business vetting. That requires a registered legal entity, a Company Page verified by its super admin, and a two-tier review with a screencast. If you're rejected you have to start over with a new app. Confirm your use case is allowed before you build.

verdict.label: Gated
verdict.timeToFirstConnection: ~15 minutes for Sign In with LinkedIn / Share on LinkedIn
verdict.timeToProduction: Weeks to months for Community Management API. LinkedIn publishes no timeline, and approval is at its discretion.
verdict.approvalWait: Two reviews (Development tier, then Standard tier). Third-party estimates range from 4 weeks to several months.
verdict.handsOnEffort: 2–4 days: entity verification, page verification, full integration, screencast

decideFirst.question: Do you only need sign-in or posting to the member's own profile?
decideFirst.guidance: If so, request Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect and Share on LinkedIn. Both are self-serve. Stop here and skip the rest of this guide.

decideFirst.question: Is your use case allowed, and are you a registered legal organization?
decideFirst.guidance: The Community Management API is only for registered legal organizations with commercial use cases, and you must check the restricted-use-case list. Personal email addresses fail vetting.

phases.name: 1 · Create the app and verify your Page
phases.goal: App linked to a real, verified Company Page
phases.duration: ~30 min + waiting for the Page admin

steps.title: Create a developer app linked to your company's LinkedIn Page
steps.detail: Don't use a placeholder or test Page. The app name and logo can't include LinkedIn or Microsoft names or logos.

steps.title: Have a Page super admin verify the app
steps.detail: Generate the verification link in app settings. A super admin of that Page must approve it.

steps.title: Add self-serve products
steps.detail: Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect and Share on LinkedIn are granted without review.

phases.name: 2 · Development tier review
phases.goal: Limited access to build and test

steps.title: Request access to Community Management API under Products
steps.detail: If the app already has other provisioned or pending products, such as the Ads API, the request option is grayed out. Use a fresh app.

steps.title: Complete the access form
steps.detail: You'll need a business email (verified), legal name, registered address, website and privacy policy, and they must all match. The agent can pre-fill the form and check for mismatches.

steps.title: LinkedIn vets your use case, organization, domain and Page verification
steps.detail: If rejected, you can't re-apply with the same app.

steps.title: Fully integrate the APIs first
steps.detail: Changing functionality after review may trigger another review.

steps.title: Record a screencast for each use case
steps.detail: High resolution and downloadable, with only your app on screen; narration is recommended. Show the full OAuth flow and each personal-data field you display. The agent can write the script.

steps.title: Submit the Standard tier form with test credentials
steps.detail: Reviewers check use case, privacy policy, data storage requirements and the screencast. A rejection here also sends you back to a new app and a new Development tier request.

requirements.item: Registered legal organization + commercial use case
App verified by a super admin of your Company Page
requirements.requiredFor: Community Management, Conversions and other gated products

blockers.cause: The app already has other products provisioned or pending
blockers.fix: Create a new app just for the Community Management request.

blockers.cause: Unsupported use case, mismatched business details, personal email, or an unverified Page
blockers.fix: Fix the qualification gap, then create a new app and submit a new Development tier request. This applies to a rejection at either tier; the old app can't re-apply.

blockers.cause: Several sources say LinkedIn no longer grants MDP to new apps
blockers.fix: Request the specific product instead, e.g. Community Management API or Advertising API.

nuances.title: API versions are retired regularly
nuances.detail: The official review page carries a notice that Marketing version 202511 is sunset on 16 Nov 2026. Pin a version and plan to upgrade.

nuances.title: A second app can reuse your Standard approval
nuances.detail: Submit another Standard tier form for the new app and give the client ID of the approved one. LinkedIn says this speeds up the review.

nuances.title: Approval can be withdrawn later
nuances.detail: LinkedIn may suspend access for non-compliance even after approval.

sources.title: LinkedIn (Microsoft Learn) — Community Management App Review
LinkedIn — Getting access to Conversions API

checked: Every Development and Standard tier requirement, the rejection and re-apply rule, and the screencast requirements, by reading LinkedIn's current (2026-10) Community Management App Review page
Re-read the same page in full on 12 Nov 2026 and compared it with the 16 claims in this guide that cite it. All held; one was made more precise (see Corrected) and one detail was added.
corrected: The first version said a rejected app can't re-apply, without saying which tier. The page says so for both tiers, and a Standard tier rejection restarts at the Development tier. The guide now says this.
Many guides still say to request the 'Marketing Developer Platform'. The current path is product-specific (Community Management API), and secondary sources report MDP is closed to new apps.
unverified: Review durations. LinkedIn publishes none; the estimates of 4 weeks to 4 months come from a third party.
That MDP is closed to new apps. This is reported by secondary sources only.
